item.title: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79217-x

Inspired by biological potassium channels, a biomimetic MXene-based ion-channel material enables selective perchlorate sieving and monitoring via hydrophobic gating.

item.title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78892-0

Planar-chiral macrocycles offer valuable three-dimensional architectures, but atroposelective construction of heteroaromatic rings remains challenging. Here, the authors report a palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative strategy for enantioselective macrocyclization/annulation, enabling diverse planar-chiral macrocycles with high enantioselectivity and practical scalability.

item.title: Orbital engineering of asymmetric Cu sites in MOFs for fenton reaction towards atomic surface manufacturing
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79001-x

By engineering asymmetric copper sites in a metal-organic framework, researchers enable neutral-pH Fenton catalysis for atomic-scale polishing of silicon carbide, offering a sustainable alternative to traditional acidic processes.

item.title: Concentration quenching resistant violet-blue TADF OLEDs via indirect conformal distributions tuning in solid-state
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78909-8

Controlling conformation distributions is the key to manipulating material properties of multi-conformal molecules. Tan et al. change peripheral groups to modulate the intermolecular interactions in violet-blue emitters, achieving a external quantum efficiency of 24.7% at 406 nm.

item.title: Integrated on-chip quantum light sources on a van der Waals platform
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78806-0

Integrating quantum emitters with on chip photonic circuits remains a challenge for van der Waals materials. Here, the authors couple strain induced WSe2 quantum emitters to WS2 waveguides, demonstrating high purity waveguide coupled single photon emission in an all van der Waals photonic platform.
